vpipe_scalar_sdpa_against_turbocider.result: attention contributes but is not the first divergence

turbocider_non_mps_bf16_linear.result: partial improvement only; still far outside parity gate and not retained

diagnostics.interpretation: Per-element dumps locate the first mismatch before main block 0: refined text already differs by 0.55% relative L2 and the first QKV input by 0.82%. Disabling TurboCider's MPSGraph BF16 linear route improves final relative L2 only from about 9.70% to 8.67%, while vpipe's scalar attention improves it only to 9.06%. The residual is therefore cumulative BF16 kernel reduction/order drift across projection, refiner, attention and MLP paths, not a row-layout, schedule, final-head or single fused-operator bug.

conclusion.memory: TurboCider admitted 14 pinned blocks under the 16 GiB target; vpipe admitted zero resident blocks and used a single streaming slot
conclusion.performance: TurboCider is approximately 1.53x faster process-wall, 1.67x faster on the first denoise, and 2.29x faster on the retained denoise request
conclusion.shipping_status: vpipe cannot replace the shipping H3 runtime
conclusion.next_required_work: A replacement runtime would need a shared arithmetic contract or matched BF16 kernels beginning with condition/patch projection and the text refiner; vpipe loading/offloading features may be ported independently, but vpipe execution must remain disabled until the existing quality gate passes.
